findings.description: TICKER SOURCING — the spec's stated mechanism vs. the code's actual one. Spec: 'write each per-row formula as references to that row's own cells.' Real code: 2 of the 7 formula columns contain ZERO cell references. `price_formula()` (lib.rs:255) emits `=GOOGLEFINANCE("{ticker}","price")` and `quote_date_formula()` (lib.rs:270) emits `=IFERROR(TEXT(INT(GOOGLEFINANCE("{ticker}","tradetime"))-DATE(1970,1,1),"0"),"")` — the ticker is an alias-resolved (`AliasMap::resolve`) quoted string LITERAL baked into the formula text, not a reference to the row's own Symbol cell A{r}. All 3 A-runs, reading the spec text alone, emitted a reference form (A1 `=GOOGLEFINANCE(B{row},"price")`; A2/A3 `GOOGLEFINANCE({sym}{r},…)` wrapped in a blank guard). All 3 B-runs, reading the code alone, pinned the literal + alias resolution as a SHALL — behavior the spec text never mentions (the word 'alias', 'ticker', and 'GOOGLEFINANCE' appear nowhere in SHEET-FORMULA-002). Consequence: the anti-mis-pairing guarantee rests on two DIFFERENT mechanisms — own-row relative refs for F/G/I/J/K, and full-range regeneration for E/M — where the spec asserts one uniform mechanism.

'EACH per-row formula' is pinned for 2 of 7 and leak-guarded for 1 of 7. `tests/formula.rs::per_row_formulas_reference_their_own_row_beneath_frozen_header` (lines 68-107) asserts own-row references only for Market Value (`E{r}`, `B{r}`) and Unrealized P&L (`F{r}`, `D{r}`); the cross-row leak loop (lines 93-105) checks only the Market Value string `mv`. Est. Unrealized Tax `=G{r}*H{r}`, Net Unrealized `=G{r}*(1-H{r})`, Unrealized % `=IF(D{r}=0,0,G{r}/D{r})`, Price and Quote Date are never leak-checked at all. The spec's universal quantifier ('each per-row formula … so a row shift cannot mis-pair them') is under-pinned: a regression that emitted `=G{r}*H{r+1}` for column I would pass the whole suite.

The anchored-range discipline (tail truncation) is enforced ONLY in the test fakes; production leaves a residual tail. `sheets-view/src/testkit.rs:178` replaces `existing.rows` wholesale, and `runtime/src/testkit.rs::update_range` does `grid.truncate(start)` before pushing — so tests always see an exactly-bounded range. Production `ViewSheetsAdapter::batch_update_view` (adapters.rs:219) writes `'{tab}'!A{DATA_START_ROW}:Z` through `SheetsApi::update_range`, which is a plain `values.update` PUT (`sheets.rs:510`) overwriting only the rows supplied — it never clears the tail, and `clear_range` (which exists, `sheets.rs:536`) is never called on this path. All 3 A-runs bound the written range to the exact row count (A1 `data_range` ends at `last`; A2 `formula_range` ends at `end`; A3 same) precisely so the anchored row set stays aligned. Failure: close a position so the tab shrinks from 5 rows to 4 — row 6 survives with its stale own-row formulas, still recalculating a live GOOGLEFINANCE price, and `read_price_pass` (which reads the same `A2:Z` and keys on column 0, adapters.rs:255-274) re-injects a mark for a symbol no longer held.

'Never-rewritten frozen header' — two production writers touch row 1, and the header is never verified. All 3 A-runs made 'only the header bootstrap ever writes a row above the anchor' structural (A1 assumption 7, A2 assumption 10, A3 assumption 1). Real code: (a) `ViewSheetsAdapter::batch_update_view` writes `'{tab}'!A1` on the missing-tab bootstrap path (adapters.rs:230); (b) `write_stale_banner` writes `'{tab}'!AA1` (adapters.rs:286) — column AA of ROW 1, i.e. inside the frozen header row though outside its A–M columns and outside the `A2:Z` data range. The spec never defines the frozen header's extent (all of row 1, or only the occupied columns) and the code silently takes the permissive column-scoped reading. Separately, the header-equality check exists only as `assert_eq!(existing.header, tab.header)` in the in-memory fake (testkit.rs:174); the production adapter never reads the existing header back, so a workbook whose row 1 was hand-edited silently gets new-schema data written under an old header.

The entire Positions column layout and formula/value split is code-side surplus. The spec names no tab, no column, and no formula. The code pins: exactly 13 columns in fixed order (`POSITIONS_HEADER`, lib.rs:174) A Symbol, B Shares, C Avg Cost/Share, D Total Basis, E Price, F Market Value, G Unrealized P&L, H Est. Tax Rate, I Est. Unrealized Tax (est), J Net Unrealized (est), K Unrealized %, L Realized P&L, M Quote Date; formulas exactly {E,F,G,I,J,K,M} and values exactly {A,B,C,D,H,L} (asserted name-by-name in `live_price_columns_are_formulas_others_are_values`); and the exact bodies `=E{r}*B{r}`, `=F{r}-D{r}`, `=G{r}*H{r}`, `=G{r}*(1-H{r})`, `=IF(D{r}=0,0,G{r}/D{r})` (lib.rs:563-574). All 3 B-runs reconstructed this identically, including the divide-by-zero tie-break (K yields 0, never #DIV/0!, when Total Basis is 0).

The formula layout is silently also a READ contract, which the spec never states. `price_reading_from_cells` (adapters.rs:297-327) hardcodes `const PRICE_COL: usize = 4` and `const QUOTE_DATE_COL: usize = 12`, keys the row by cell 0 (Symbol), and defaults an unparseable/missing quote date to `Date(0)` — 1970-01-01 — rather than degrading the reading. So a Positions column reorder that the spec would permit silently mis-reads prices and stamps every mark with the epoch. All 3 B-runs pinned cols 4 and 12; B1 and B2 pinned the `Date(0)` default. Also code-side-only: `#N/A` and empty both map to `Transient`, any other `#`-prefixed cell maps to `Permanent`, a non-`#` unparseable cell maps to `Permanent`.

`DATA_START_ROW = 2` and 'header is exactly one row'. The spec says 'a fixed anchored start row beneath a never-rewritten frozen header' and names neither value. The code makes 2 a public constant (lib.rs:148) consumed by `runtime`'s `data_range` and by the settle-pass range, and the test hard-pins it with `assert_eq!(DATA_START_ROW, 2)` (formula.rs:77). Benign in that all 3 A-runs independently guessed 2 — but the spec grants no license for a multi-row or spacer header, and A2 built `header_rows`/`anchor_row` as separate configurable fields with an `AnchorInsideHeader` error because the spec left it open.

The Est. Tax Rate (H) encoding and its degradation path are load-bearing and entirely unstated. `fmt_ppm` (lib.rs:497) emits `{whole}.{frac:04}%` — exactly four fractional digits, signed, e.g. `20.0000%` — as a `Cell::Value`, which reaches Sheets via `valueInputOption=USER_ENTERED` (sheets.rs:511) so it coerces to the numeric fraction 0.20 that `=G{r}*H{r}` and `=G{r}*(1-H{r})` multiply. When a symbol has no effective rate the cell is the EMPTY STRING (`eff_rate.map(fmt_ppm).unwrap_or_default()`, lib.rs:585), so `=G*H` silently evaluates to 0 and `=G*(1-H)` to G: a degraded estimate renders as 'Est. Unrealized Tax 0.00', indistinguishable from a genuinely zero tax. All 3 B-runs raised this to a SHALL (B2 even added a `[0,1]` finiteness bound that only the test models, formula.rs:184-187). None of it is in the spec text.

`ViewError::DuplicateSymbolRow(symbol)` — `render_positions` aborts the entire tab if two rows carry one symbol (lib.rs:540-545). All 3 B-runs elevated this to a SHALL / Unwanted-behavior clause and tied it to read-back row identity. The spec text mentions no error semantics at all. Note the code itself documents the guard as structurally UNREACHABLE through the real API (`Snapshot.positions` is a `Map<Symbol,_>`), so B-side reconstructions are pinning a defensive branch as required behavior.

Range shape and formula-free siblings. The write and the settle read both address `'{tab}'!A{DATA_START_ROW}:Z` (adapters.rs:200, 255) — column-unbounded to Z for a 13-column tab; the spec states only 'from a fixed anchored start row' and constrains no column extent. Separately, `tax_tab_is_kernel_exact_not_live_formula` asserts that Open Lots, Realized, and BOTH Tax bands contain zero formula cells; all 3 B-runs stated this as a requirement. The spec never says which tabs may carry per-row formulas.

notes:
Files read: crates/sheets-view/src/lib.rs, crates/sheets-view/src/testkit.rs, crates/sheets-view/tests/formula.rs, crates/runtime/src/adapters.rs, plus crates/runtime/src/sheets.rs and crates/runtime/src/testkit.rs (needed to check whether the fake's tail-truncate and USER_ENTERED claims hold in production).

Verified rather than assumed: (1) `valueInputOption=USER_ENTERED` IS real in production (sheets.rs:511), so the Est. Tax Rate percent-coercion contract the B-runs pinned does hold end-to-end — the drift there is that the spec never states it, not that it is broken. (2) Tail truncation is NOT real in production — `runtime/src/testkit.rs::update_range` does `grid.truncate(start)` but `sheets.rs:510` is a plain values.update PUT and `clear_range` is never called from the view path. That asymmetry is what makes finding 3 a genuine defect rather than a documentation nit.

A-side assumption artifacts EXCLUDED from the findings (unanimous or near-unanimous A-side behavior with no basis in the spec text): blank-symbol/error guards `IF(sym="","",…)` / `IFERROR(...)` around the price formula (A2, A3 — the real code has IFERROR on Quote Date only, none on Price); row-index overflow as an explicit error or panic (all 3 A-runs; the real code does an unchecked `(rows.len() as u32) + DATA_START_ROW` at lib.rs:546); the Sheets 10M-row cap (A1 only); `n_rows == 0` degenerate-range handling (all 3, but see finding 3 — the real gap there is truncation, not the empty case); configurable `header_rows > 1` with an `AnchorInsideHeader` error (A2 only).

Worth noting for the arrow: all 3 A-runs independently and explicitly REJECTED `$`-absolute row references, reasoning that `$D$5` is exactly the mis-pairing bug the spec forbids while same-row relative refs are what survives a shift. The real code agrees (plain `E2`, `B2`). That is the one substantive sub-decision the spec leaves open where both directions converged — a rare coherent spot in an otherwise heavily drifted requirement.

Classification rationale: BD-DRIFT rather than B-ONLY-DRIFT. The B-side surplus is large and unanimous (the spec sentence is ~40 words; the code pins a 13-column schema, 7 formula bodies, a read-back index contract, a percent-coercion contract, and an error variant). But the A-side is not merely inventing — finding 1 traces directly to the spec's own phrase 'as references to that row's own cells' and is contradicted by 2 of 7 real formula columns, and findings 3 and 4 trace to 'from a fixed anchored start row beneath a never-rewritten frozen header'. Finding 1 is the BD convergence point: both directions land on the same locus (how a per-row formula obtains its ticker) from opposite sides.
